title: Philips 50PUS8517/12 (50" 4K UHD LED, 3-sided Ambilight, P5 Picture Engine, 2022 model)
header:
Philips 50PUS8517/12 (50" 4K UHD LED, 3-sided Ambilight, P5 Picture Engine, 2022 model)
Android TV 11 (ro.build.version.release=11), firmware RTT2.211108.001, board PH1M_EA_9970A
ro.product.model=2021_22_Philips_UHD_Android_TV  ro.product.device=PH1M_EA_9970A
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/21029:user/release-keys
TP Vision build: MediaTek MT5895, 2.67 GB RAM, armeabi-v7a userspace. Vendor packages use the
org.droidtv prefix.

Match on the BOARD and firmware, not on the model number. Philips/TP Vision ships one
org.droidtv layer across a whole generation, so the x PUS85xx / PUS88xx sets of 2021-2022 on
board PH1M_EA_9970A should carry the same package set; a different board or a Google TV
(Android 12+) Philips will not. Check your own `pm list packages` against this file first —
`tools/tv.py --probe` prints model, Android version and build.

NOT the same platform as examples/philips-smart-4k-google-tv, which is a Skyworth-built
India-market set on Google TV 14 with com.smartdevice/com.sky/com.tianci packages and no
org.droidtv at all. Nothing from that file applies here and nothing here applies there.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (pass it to restore.sh, as above).
Live TV app:    org.droidtv.playtv
App labels below were resolved by pulling each APK and reading it with `aapt dump badging`,
not guessed from the package name. That matters on this firmware: org.droidtv.nettvapp4546 is
MEGOGO, nettvapp4655 is Deezer, nettvapp5512 is Fishing TV, and org.droidtv.candeebug is
labelled "DAC" and is the analytics uploader, not a debug tool.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE, in the order they will bite you:

1. pm disable-user persists to /data/system/users/0/package-restrictions.xml with a delay
(~10 s on AOSP). If you run disable.sh and power-cycle the TV straight away, the changes
are silently lost: packages come back as enabled=0 (DEFAULT). Wait, or run
`pm list packages -d` and confirm your packages are listed before pulling the plug.
2. `adb reboot` over TCP hangs holding the dropped connection. Kill the adb server right
after sending it and wait on port 5555 coming back instead of on the adb command.
3. The Android 11 shell cannot disable individual components of another app
("SecurityException: Shell cannot change component state") and cannot `pm hide`
("Neither user 2000 nor current process has android.permission.MANAGE_USERS"). So if a
package refuses to stay disabled, the shell has no second lever. `pm suspend` does work
and survives a reboot, but it does not stop services: an app that starts itself from its
own boot receiver keeps running with suspended=true.
4. com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast built-in) could NOT be kept disabled on this
firmware and is deliberately absent from the list below. It returns to enabled=1 about 35 s
after every boot, reproducibly. pm disable-user, pm suspend, per-component disable and
pm hide were all tried; the first is undone, the second does not stop it, the last two are
refused by the platform. Left enabled, at a cost of about 37 MB.
5. A DISABLED PACKAGE CAN LEAVE A PERSISTENT PROCESS RETRYING FOREVER, AND pidof WILL NOT
SHOW IT. org.droidtv.xtv is the persistent TV engine and has five outbound service
bindings. Two of them, eum and aurora, were on the first version of this list, and
BOTH leave xtv in a permanent retry loop when disabled. Neither is in the list above now;
both are in the DO NOT DISABLE block below.

org.droidtv.eum -- bound via CONTEXTUALHELP. About five retries per second, logged as
xtvContextInterface ... connectCotextService - Service failed to connec i is null
51 of them in 10 seconds of an idle TV. This one also BREAKS A VISIBLE FUNCTION, and not
the one you would guess: the Philips sources drawer opens and vanishes within a second,
so HDMI inputs stop being reachable from the remote's SOURCES key. SourcesService logged
a correct, complete source list every time and the drawer still died.

org.droidtv.aurora -- about five retries per second too, logged as
xtvService: xtvService handleConnectAurora
at a steady 201 ms interval, 59 in 30 seconds of an idle TV. This one breaks nothing
visible and costs little: xtv sits at 0.2% of one core while doing it. It is log noise
plus a retry that can never succeed. Re-enabling it is free in practice -- aurora's
process does not start at idle even when the package is enabled, so xtv only needed the
package to be resolvable.

`pm enable` on either took its counter to zero immediately, with no reboot.

THE METHOD, which is the transferable part: a live PID proves the process exists, not
that it is healthy. xtv held the same PID through all eleven batches while both loops
ran. And do not grep for a string you already know -- that is how I missed the second
loop for a day after fixing the first. Clear the log, wait 30 seconds on an idle TV,
then group EVERYTHING by frequency and look at what repeats:
adb shell logcat -c; sleep 30; adb shell logcat -d > idle.txt
# then collapse digits and count: anything repeating several times a second is a loop
On this set that takes an idle log from 130 lines per 30 s down to 50, and the 50 that
remain are the firmware's own heartbeats.
6. The replacement launcher takes over on its own. Projectivy declares
android.intent.category.HOME, so the moment com.google.android.tvlauncher is disabled the
system resolves HOME to it — immediately, without a reboot and without enabling any
accessibility service. Check with
`cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME`
BEFORE disabling the stock launcher, and make sure your replacement is listed by
`cmd package query-activities` for that intent. If it is not, you will be left without a
home screen (see issue #90).

sections.title: TP Vision telemetry

apps.note: "DAC" analytics uploader: channel watched, resolution, HDMI-CEC devices, viewing times, Ambilight config; uploads to AWS Firehose/S3 and geolocates the public IP via ipinfo.io
metrics collector sharing candeebug's process; no INTERNET permission of its own
boot stats, remote keypress counts, panel/eMMC telemetry forwarded to the above

sections.note: org.droidtv.gel runs inside the candeebug process (android:process="org.droidtv.candeebug"), so disabling candeebug alone leaves a process with that name still running and looks like a failure. Disable both.

sections.title: Philips content promos and the app gallery

apps.note: its headless backend; disable the row above first or you get a live tile with no data source

sections.title: Philips features this owner does not use

apps.note: Alexa bridge; live TV holds a binding into it, so test channel zapping and the EPG after disabling -- NOT exercised on this unit

DLNA/UPnP server and renderer; persistent + coreApp, yet disables cleanly and contentexplorer ("Media") still starts and keeps its PID. Its DLNA init is gated behind a broadcast dlna itself sends, so the USB source should be unaffected -- reasoned from the code, not tested here

LAN control of volume, audio output, Ambilight on/off and ShopMode. NOTE: this is NOT the JointSpace API on ports 1925/1926 — that is served by org.droidtv.xtv, which must stay. Keep this if you drive the TV from Home Assistant
"Demo me" retail demo mode, e-sticker and shop loop; bound at boot by org.droidtv.settings to clear demo clips before a firmware update, null-guarded
M7 satellite operator promo (Canal Digitaal, TV Vlaanderen, Skylink, HD Austria); keep if you use one of those

Second Screen Setup Auth Bridge (set-up-from-phone helper)

apps.note: Assistant and voice search, ~101 MB across two processes. Kills the remote's mic button, "Hey Google", on-screen voice search and the mic icon inside YouTube and Play Store search. Settings and tvsystemui guard their calls into it, so nothing crashes
TalkBack screen reader; keep if anyone needs it

apps.note: Vodafone TV; runs headless, no icon

optional.note: launcher/build-and-install.sh disables the stock launcher itself, after Home has moved # 190 MB resident, the single heaviest process on this TV

sections.note: All of these sit in /data/app rather than on the system partition, so unlike the vendor packages above they are ordinary user-installed apps.

sections.title: Stock launcher and its content engine, replaced by launcher/ (or Projectivy)

apps.note: "Android TV Core Services" despite the name: recommendation rows, channels, notification panel

sections.note: ORDER MATTERS: disable the launcher FIRST. com.google.android.tvlauncher holds a stable ContentProvider reference on tvrecommendations/.NotificationContentProvider, and ActivityManagerService kills a client holding a stable ref when the provider's process dies — so disabling tvrecommendations first force-stops the live 190 MB launcher process. tvrecommendations is also the only resolver for the system notification panel (OPEN_NOTIFICATIONS_PANEL and friends), so that panel is gone device-wide, not just from the stock home screen. That is a conscious trade, not a side effect.

sections.title: Stock YouTube, replaced by SmartTube (ads and sponsor segments)
sections.note: 119 MB resident vs ~35 MB. Philips remotes of this generation often carry a dedicated YouTube key, which is bound to this package and will stop doing anything. The remote on this particular unit has no such key, so that was not a factor here -- check your own before you decide this matters.
